exactDomain.coordinateSine: Modulo remainder k*2^-22; off-Q22 positive remainder[0,2) has a separate complete composition table, other actual remainders fall on the captured Q22/Q19 phase nodes. Unsupported mathematical inputs are errors.
exactDomain.gradientSine: Q19 orQ22 phase nodes; positive arguments[.25,4); positive k*2^-25 arguments below.25; independently enumerated tiny positive argument interval[2^-26,2^-13). Non-covered arbitrary f32 inputs remain explicitly unsupported.
exactDomain.rsqrt: All positive binary32 values in[2^-48,4). Complete normalized[1,4) mantissa table and powers-of-four identity checked exhaustively at every exponent -48..1 (419430400 values). Raw zero vectors are rejected, matching the native invalid/NaN condition rather than replacing them with zero.

operationGraph: Every listed arithmetic edge rounds to binary32 unless FMA is explicitly stated. Fixed seed0 plan remains the SHA-bound18 independent mathematical parameters.
Coordinate dot = fma(integer_y,78.233,RN32(integer_x*12.9898)).
Modulo quotient = floor(RN32(dot*RN32(1/3.14159))); IEEE division here is observably different at four holdout lattice points.
Remainder = fma(-quotient,3.14159,dot). Its exact binary lattice is k*2^-22.

Coordinate sine composition reduces cycles = RN32(remainder * f32_bits(0x3edd8161)). This is the compiler-folded 2.71828*INV_TAU constant. Do not pass RN32(remainder*2.71828) to a generic sine primitive.
Scramble = fract(fma(coordinate_wave,438.5453,1.73205)).

Common = RN32(seed*scramble). Combined weightj = fma(common,weight_scale_j,RN32(weight_bias_j+312)). The identity graph folds +312 into the FMA bias; a runtime quantize branch changes this graph and is excluded from the current oracle.
Gradient direction coefficients = RN32(direction*planned_frequency), then dot = fma(integer_y,coefficient_y,RN32(integer_x*coefficient_x)). Argument is dot/16 through two exact*.25 scalings.
Gradient sine uses ordinary captured unary reduction. All coefficients have denominators at most2^21, so all gradient sine arguments are k*2^-25.
Product = RN32(wave*combined_weight). Centered fraction is RN32(2*RN32(RN32(product-.5)-floor(product))); do not subtract .5 after forming fract(product).
Norm squared = fma(raw_y,raw_y,RN32(raw_x*raw_x)); norm reciprocal is captured fast::rsqrt, not1/f32_sqrt. Each output = RN32(raw_component*reciprocal).
Complete displacement starts q*the already-rounded binary32 reciprocal noise-size uniform. Public q/noise_size division is not equivalent for non-dyadic sizes.
Cubic easing, dot interpolation, three octave amplitudes1/.5/.25 and final radius multiplication are included in the continuous displacement verification.
